body: Benchmark integration/composite_bench_test.go BenchmarkComposite_OneStatementVsAccessors (2026-10-07, Apple M1 Max, go1.27.1, -count 3, local engines). Same user read two ways: LoadUser with the phone and username LEFT joins (1 statement) vs LoadUserColumns + phone.Of + username.Of (3 statements). SQLite (in-process): composite 84-88us/294 allocs, accessors 86-94us/345 allocs, no real difference because there is no round trip. Postgres (Postgres.app, localhost): composite 71-88us/316 allocs, accessors 149-321us/369 allocs, about 2x. MySQL (container 127.0.0.1:33070): composite 1.0-1.5ms/289 allocs, accessors 2.6ms/350 allocs, about 2.5x. Conclusion: the cost is one round trip per accessor, so the composite query wins on any networked engine and ties on SQLite; bytes per op are equal (17.5-18.6KB). Run: go test -mod=mod -run ^$ -bench Composite ./integration with the test:engines DSNs.
